correctness.rationale: The world frame is C_n (n>=1) ordered by n|m, including C_1; each atom is an arbitrary fixed parameter-free first-order group sentence. Baur–Monk elimination for abelian groups reduces sentences to finite Boolean combinations of indices of pp-definable subgroups. For a unary pp system, Smith normal form on the quantified variables yields subgroup L(n)C_n, where local exponent contributions are eventually either constant or valuation minus constant; hence finitely many capped p-valuations plus a small-size cutoff determine any finite sentence list. The explicit finite poset with exceptional small s_n and large capped valuation tuples ell_t is directed, antisymmetric, and a surjective bounded-morphism image; back arrows lift by multiplying missing prime powers, using a fresh prime for n>N. Every finite FO valuation is its pullback, giving Grz.2 validity by soundness on finite directed posets. Conversely first-order p-torsion sentences beta_i define independent prime-divisibility coordinates and ALL Boolean-cube valuations; quotient g_r(n) onto P([r]) is a bounded morphism. Wołoszyn's Theorem 18 characterizes Grz.2 by finite Boolean lattices, proving the reverse bound. Pinned verify.py was read and confirms representative finite quotients/pp ratios; its finite tests alone do not prove the infinite Baur–Monk lemma.
